issues.failure_explanation: The Nitsche bilinear form a(u,v) defined in (1) contains boundary integrals of normal derivatives on Gamma_D. For general functions u in H^1(Omega), grad(u) belongs only to (L^2(Omega))^d and has no well-defined trace on the boundary, so a(u,v) is ill-defined on H^1(Omega) x H^1(Omega). Furthermore, a(.,.) cannot be continuous or coercive on H^1(Omega) for any constant penalty parameter C_pen > 0: boundary-layer test functions u_delta(x) = exp(-dist(x, Gamma_D)/delta) satisfy a(u_delta, u_delta) < 0 for sufficiently small delta while ||u_delta||_{H^1}^2 > 0. Consequently, Céa's Lemma cannot be applied to the weak formulation (2) on V = H^1(Omega).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must formulate Nitsche's method in an appropriate mesh-dependent broken norm or on a subspace with higher regularity, scale the penalty parameter appropriately with the mesh norm (C_pen ~ 1/h), establish discrete inverse trace inequalities for the kernel ansatz spaces, and re-derive the error bounds using a non-conforming or Strang-type analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem 4 fails because the hypotheses of Céa's Lemma on V = H^1(Omega) are violated by the Nitsche formulation. As a result, the a priori H^1 and L^2 error bounds for the kernel approximation are unproven.
issues.title: Nitsche bilinear form is not well-defined, continuous, or coercive on H^1
issues.why_classification: Resolving the failure of Céa's Lemma on H^1(Omega) requires establishing discrete inverse trace estimates for RBF spaces, scaling C_pen with h, and developing a completely new non-conforming proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: In general, the continuity constant gamma is at least as large as the coercivity constant alpha, and typically gamma > 2*alpha. When gamma >= 2*alpha, the denominator alpha - gamma/2 is non-positive, meaning dividing by it flips the inequality and results in an invalid negative upper bound on a squared norm, as well as the square root of a negative quantity in Proposition 1. The proof erroneously bounded (1/2)*a(u_h - u~_h, u_h - u~_h) by (gamma/2)*||u_h - u~_h||_V^2 on the right-hand side instead of subtracting it from the left-hand side, where the identity I(u~_h) - I(u_h) = (1/2)*a(u_h - u~_h, u_h - u~_h) >= (alpha/2)*||u_h - u~_h||_V^2 holds directly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the identity I(u~_h) - I(u_h) = (1/2)*a(u_h - u~_h, u_h - u~_h) combined with coercivity a(v,v) >= alpha*||v||_V^2 to establish ||u_h - u~_h||_V^2 <= (2/alpha)*(I(u~_h) - I(u_h)), replacing the denominator alpha - gamma/2 by alpha/2 in Lemma 1 and Proposition 1.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 are false or ill-defined whenever gamma >= 2*alpha.
issues.title: Invalid denominator alpha - gamma/2 in inexact optimization error bound
issues.why_classification: A routine two-line algebraic correction fixes the derivation, removes the invalid denominator, and restores Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 with no loss of content.
